name: Los Arcos - El Bajo del Cristo

tags.notes: Re-audited 2026-08-26: sub-site name confirmed in aggregate Los Arcos coverage (referenced as "Bajo de Cristo"). No factual changes required.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: confirmed as "Devil's Mouth"/"Devil's Canyon" wall (La Quijada del Diablo), drop-off ~18m to 25-37m, manta ray sightings corroborated. Sources disagree sharply on the scale of the adjacent trench/wall: bocadivers.net cites a ~1600 ft (488m) drop, banderas-scuba.com describes a canyon "believed to reach 1,600 meters," and other operators describe an ~800 ft (244m) wall or "over a mile" drop into the Banderas Trench. Description now flags this as an unresolved range rather than asserting one figure.

Deep wreck re-audit 2026-08-26 (requirement 4): Grounding (Feb 16, 2017) and intentional sinking (Oct 24, 2017) cross-confirmed by Banderas Scuba Republic and independent local news outlet Reporte Diario Vallarta (2 non-dive-shop-affiliated sources). CONFLICT FLAGGED: PADI's dive-site page instead states the wreck has rested at the site "since 2016" -- this contradicts the Feb/Oct 2017 grounding-and-sinking timeline and is noted as an unresolved discrepancy in the description rather than silently overwritten. No source (including a targeted search for Spanish-language 2017 sinking coverage) provides the vessel's length, tonnage, or build date, so none is stated -- description explicitly acknowledges this is undocumented rather than inventing figures. One source (divinglore.com) gives an unverified ~90ft/27m length figure with no second source corroborating it, so it is NOT included per the 2-source rule for wreck dimensions. No Wikipedia article exists for this vessel. Accompanying-wreck count varies 10-11 (PADI) to up to 14 (Banderas Scuba); kept as a 10-14 range to cover both. Goliath grouper sighting is single-sourced (banderas-scuba.com) but is a marine-life claim (1-source threshold), not a historical fact, so it is retained.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: depth range, eagle rays, scorpionfish, moray eels, and shore-entry practicality all re-confirmed. CITATION CORRECTED: bocadivers.net and banderas-scuba.com, previously listed, do not name Mismaloya as a distinct site on re-check and were removed; replaced with zentacle.com. Only 3 domains could be confirmed as genuinely site-specific -- flagged as thin sourcing.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: electric rays and stingrays confirmed site-specific (banderas-scuba.com product page + puertovallarta.net). MARINE LIFE CORRECTED: "bat rays" removed -- no source confirms this species at Colomitos specifically; it appears to have been carried over from a general Los Arcos ScubaBoard thread rather than a Colomitos-specific report.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: garden eels, jawfish, two trails, sunken panga boats, and pufferfish/seahorses all strongly re-confirmed against current vallarta-adventures.com and getyourguide.com listings. No factual changes required.
Re-audited 2026-08-26: Cortez garden eel colony re-confirmed (banderas-scuba.com: "underwater grass field" of garden eels). No factual changes required.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: UNRESOLVED SOURCING. On re-check, banderas-scuba.com and scubaboard.com (both previously listed) do not name Quimixto as a distinct dive site -- only Quimixto village/beach appears in general searches. Only 1 genuinely site-specific source could be confirmed. Content is left as-is (consistent with the region's general character) but should be treated as lower-confidence until 2 more site-specific sources are found. Flagged in QA summary per requirement 1 -- not padded with weak sources.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: manta rays, three named zones (Potrerillo/Torrecillas/Iglesias), 50-dive minimum, and moray eels all re-confirmed. MARINE LIFE CORRECTED: "occasional hammerhead or bull shark" removed -- no source, including bocadivers.net's dedicated Chimo listing, confirms sharks at this site specifically. bocadivers.net additionally confirms dolphins and occasional whales at Chimo, which have been added.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: UNRESOLVED SOURCING / SITE IDENTITY UNCERTAIN. Extensive re-search found "Las Gemelas" used consistently in current sources as a BEACH name (Playas Gemelas, near the Princesa Vallarta wreck coordinates ~3km away) rather than as a distinct twin-pinnacle dive site. No source independently confirms a "twin submerged rock formation" dive site by this name, or the cup coral / sea fan marine life previously attributed to it. banderas-scuba.com and scubaboard.com, previously cited, do not name it. Description rewritten to remove unconfirmed site-specific marine life per anti-hallucination policy; flagged prominently in QA summary as needing a fresh on-the-ground source before the next validation pass.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: National Park date (Feb 2 2004), UNESCO designation (2008), humpback whale season (Dec-Mar), and manta ray/turtle sightings all re-confirmed against dresseldivers.com's Punta Mita page. No factual changes required.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: nurse sharks now independently confirmed by sayulitaentourage.com ("sometimes even nurse sharks") in addition to banderas-scuba.com. Cave/swimthrough network and position between Marietas and El Morro re-confirmed. No factual changes required.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: whale shark (early summer), humpback whale (winter), sailfish, and marlin seasonal claims all re-confirmed against current operator pages. banderas-scuba.com also lists white-tip sharks and sea lions at this site, now added. No other factual changes required.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: reef sharks, nurse sharks, and hammerhead/whitetip shark sightings now cross-confirmed by vallarta-adventures.com's shark blog in addition to greatestdivesites.com. Boat transit (~2 hours), 36nm distance, 25-dive minimum re-confirmed.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: 300m mesa ("underwater sportsfield"/"football field"), 18-25m depth, sailfish, and tuna schools strongly re-confirmed across independent operator pages. MARINE LIFE CORRECTED: "hammerhead sharks patrol the deeper flanks" softened to a generic, unattributed shark mention -- no source names hammerheads at El Sequial specifically (hammerheads are attributed to the neighboring Corbeteña, not El Sequial, by available sources).

Re-audited 2026-08-26: two-depth structure (12m/30m) confirmed exactly by dresseldivers.com's dive planner. Cave/tunnel and technical-diving character confirmed by banderas-scuba.com. No factual changes required.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: CITATION CORRECTED -- puertovallartatours.net, previously cited, describes a DIFFERENT site also named "La Puntilla" located at Mismaloya (south bay, shore-accessible, sandy bottom, zebra moray eels, baby stingrays) that does not match this entry's coordinates or boat-access-only Punta de Mita location. That citation has been removed. dresseldivers.com's Punta de Mita dive planner independently confirms the exact two-depth structure (22m/73ft and 12m/40ft) already in this entry, which is strong corroboration of the depth data specifically, but only 1 genuinely site-specific domain could be confirmed. UNRESOLVED SOURCING per requirement 1 -- flagged in QA summary, not padded with weak sources. Name-sharing with the Mismaloya site should be watched for on future validation passes.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: CITATION CORRECTED -- puertovallartatours.net, previously cited, does not mention Love Rocks at all; removed. dresseldivers.com independently confirms 10m/33ft depth (exact match) and the heart-shaped-rock naming origin with porcupine fish and goatfish, now added to the description. Only 1 genuinely site-specific domain confirmed. UNRESOLVED SOURCING per requirement 1 -- flagged in QA summary, not padded with weak sources.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: muddy-sand bottom, sponges, nudibranchs, and location west of La Cruz de Huanacaxtle strongly re-confirmed verbatim against puertovallarta.net. banderas-scuba.com and scubaboard.com, previously listed, do not name Las Viudas specifically and have been removed. Only 2 genuinely site-specific domains confirmed. UNRESOLVED SOURCING per requirement 1 -- flagged in QA summary.

Re-audited 2026-08-26: sea snakes, moray eels, 1h20m transit, and 21-40m depth range re-confirmed verbatim against puertovallarta.net. banderas-scuba.com, boca divers, and scubaboard.com, previously listed, do not name Pizota specifically and have been removed. Only 1 genuinely site-specific domain confirmed. UNRESOLVED SOURCING per requirement 1 -- flagged in QA summary, not padded with weak sources.
